title: Beyond the 956: Woman handcuffed by NYPD after scattering street vendors' bags near Rockefeller Center

content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A woman was placed in handcuffs by New York City police officers after she scattered handbags from a street vendor display near Rockefeller Center in Midtown Manhattan, according to video posted by WorldStar on Sunday, November 22.

The video shows the woman approaching a white sheet spread on the sidewalk with purses and tote bags displayed for sale and scattering the merchandise. Officers then arrived and placed her in handcuffs, and the vendors were seen gathering their goods and leaving the area, according to the reports.

The vendors were displaying suspected counterfeit designer bags, WorldStar reported. It has not been independently established whether the woman was formally arrested or charged, and her name has not been publicly reported.

New York City Council Member Vickie Paladino reacted to the footage, questioning the police response and arguing that the system appeared to protect sellers of counterfeit merchandise rather than address the underlying activity, according to GhanaNews24.

The incident has renewed debate over illegal street vending in some of New York's busiest commercial and tourist areas, where residents and business owners have complained that makeshift displays block sidewalks and shop entrances.
